Wrong number

y₁ = Tₙ/11.4
y₂ = (Tₙ+7)/11.4

Equation details

T=(0,0,rest,rest,4,4,rest,7,rest,rest,rest,rest), rate=3.5. Two sine voices ring in paired bursts. On cells n mod 12 >= 7, ring modulation multiplies them by 173 Hz and 227 Hz sine waves. This is a toy telephone gesture, not a DTMF encoder. Unless specified otherwise, u=rate(x+8−offset), n=floor(u), r=frac(u); notes repeat modulo list length. Voice 2: rate=3.5; offset=0; gate=0.72; decay=0.3; root=392 Hz; voice=Sine.

Popcorn panic

yⱼ = [Pⱼ−22r]/11.4; r=(x−tⱼ)/dⱼ

Equation details

Event gaps start at 1.1 and multiply by 0.88 down to 0.11; each four-unit section restarts the acceleration. Durations are 0.08 to 0.16 units. Seeded pentatonic pitches and gains; overlapping sin²-windowed chirplets. Unless specified otherwise, u=rate(x+8−offset), n=floor(u), r=frac(u); notes repeat modulo list length. Each active cell has a smooth attack and release, with exp(−decay*r) loudness. Pitch is in semitones divided by 11.4. Voice 1: seeded events

Synthesis references

  • Barry Truax: Frequency Modulation Synthesis - FM ratios and changing modulation index informed the synthetic duck, tuba, sneeze and typewriter timbres. These are original caricatures, not instrument models or recordings.
  • Stanford CCRMA: FM synthesis - Phase modulation of a sine carrier; the Vivid renderer uses a bounded modulation index.
  • Barry Truax: Granular synthesis - Short windowed sound particles informed Popcorn panic.
  • Csound: Amplitude and ring modulation - Signal multiplication informed the alien and telephone timbres.

Ring modulation multiplies the synthesized waveform by a sine oscillator, blended with the dry waveform: output = input[(1−d)+d sin(φ)], φ accumulates 2πf/sampleRate. Wrong number and Alien gargle specify their own f and d. All note schedules and curves are original. Existing 109 patterns remain available; this addition brings the collection to 123.
